ok.snippet:
_**Quercus garryana**_ is an [oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak) tree species found most commonly in the [Pacific Northwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Northwest), with a range stretching from southern [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California) to southwestern [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia). [[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-6) It is commonly known as the **Garry oak, Oregon white oak** or **Oregon oak**.

## Description
[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Quercus_garryana&action=edit&section=1)]

_Quercus garryana_ is typically of medium height, growing slowly to around 80 feet (24 metres) and occasionally as high as 100ft (30m), or in [shrub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrub) form to 10 to 15ft (3.0 to 4.6m) tall. [[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) It has the characteristic oval profile of other [oaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak) when solitary, but is also known to grow in groves close enough together that crowns may form a canopy. The [fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit) a small [acorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acorn)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-9)3⁄4–1in (19–25mm) long, rarely 1+1⁄2 in, and 1⁄2–3⁄4in (13–19mm) broad, with shallow, scaly cups.

[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-10) They are attached to the undersides of leaves.

The Garry Oak ( _Quercus garryana_), also called Oregon white oak, ranges from British Columbia to California. The latin scientific name, _Quercus garryana_, was bestowed by Botanist David Douglas in the early 1800's to honor his friend, Nicholas Garry, an officer in the Hudson Bay Trading Company. The Garry oak ( _Quercus garryana_) is one of 20 native oak species found on the Pacific Coast of Northern America, but the only native oak found in western Washington or British Columbia.

- [![The shrub-like form of Oregon white oak (Quercus garryana var. breweri) growing in serpentine soils in southwest Oregon.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Quercus_garryana_var_breweri.jpg/330px-Quercus_garryana_var_breweri.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Quercus_garryana_var_breweri.jpg)

The shrub-like form of Oregon white oak ( _Quercus garryana_ var. _breweri_) growing in serpentine soils in southwest Oregon.

## Ecology
### _Quercus garryana_ woodlands
_Quercus garryana_ woodlands create a landscape mosaic of grassland, savanna, woodland, and closed-canopy forest. [[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-28) It grows in a variety of soil types, for instance, rocky outcrops, glacial gravelly outwash, deep grassland soils, and seasonally flooded riparian areas. [[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Dunn_and_Ewing-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Lea-26)

Livestock grazing trampled and consumed oak seedlings. [[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Dunn_and_Ewing-25) On Vancouver Island, more than 90% was gone,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Lea-26) and on Whidbey Island up to 99% of native understory Oregon white oak habitat is gone. [[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-29) Remaining Oregon white oak woodlands are threatened by urbanization, conversion to Douglas-fir woodland, and invasion by shrubs, both native and nonnative (Scotch broom _[Cytisus scoparius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytisus_scoparius)_, sweetbriar rose _[Rosa eglanteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosa_eglanteria)_, snowberry _[Symphoricarpos albus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphoricarpos_albus)_, Indian plum _[Oemleria cerasiformis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oemleria_cerasiformis)_, poison-oak _[Toxicodendron diversilobum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxicodendron_diversilobum)_, English holly _[Ilex aquifolium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilex_aquifolium)_, bird cherry _[Prunus avium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prunus_avium)_). [[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Dunn_and_Ewing-25)

[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-host-31)

## Uses
[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-Audubon-8)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:0-39) The bitterness of the toxic [tannic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tannic_acid) would likely prevent anyone from eating enough to become ill.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:0-39) [Native Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas) ate the acorns raw and roasted, also using them to make a kind of flour.

[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-40) Although it was popularly used around the turn of the 20th century,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-:022-7) historically the tree has not been regarded as having significant commercial value and is frequently destroyed as land is cleared for development. [[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-41) In Washington, it has been used for aging [single malt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_malt_whisky) [whiskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whiskey) since the 2010s. [[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_garryana#cite_note-43) Oregon white oak barrels are said to give the whiskey "burnt sugar notes, marshmallow sweetness, and a light floral character that showcases the best of the Garry oak".

# Oregon White Oak
_Quercus garryana_ Dougl. ex Hook.

#### Introduction
Oregon white oak _(Quercus garryana)_, a broadleaved deciduous hardwood common inland along the Pacific Coast, has the longest north-south distribution among western oaks-from Vancouver Island, British Columbia, to southern California.

### Management with Natural Regeneration
#### Genetics
_Quercus garryana_ hybridizes naturally with four other oaks.
